sections.topic: Big data, cloud computing, edge computing and data centres
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 5 Science, Tech & Environment › 19 › Big data, cloud computing, edge computing and data centres › Universal angles
bullets: Current relevance: Data-centre capacity reached 1.57 GW (2026) (LENSD 17 Sep 2026). The ES 2025-26 says rising data-centre capacity enables cloud, AI, IoT and 5G.
AP angle: Vizag is projected to become India's biggest data-centre hub, ~6 GW over 10 years (TH 2 Jan 2026).
Criticism & debates: Power and water strain from hyperscale centres. India relies on foreign cloud providers for AI compute (LENS Jul 2026).

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 5 Science, Tech & Environment › 19 › Artificial intelligence and machine learning - concepts, applications, national AI strategy, ethical concerns › Ethical concerns - bias, deepfakes, privacy, facial recognition, jobs, explainability
bullets: Bias comes from training data that is not representative. Health AI trained on urban/Western data misses India's diversity (LENS Aug 2026). Facial-recognition accuracy varies with lighting, pose and demographics.
Deepfakes are made with GANs, diffusion models and large neural nets, and come as text, voice, image or video.
Privacy and surveillance: identification without consent, mass surveillance, predictive policing that threatens due process.
Job displacement in both manual and intellectual work. Explainability: deep models are "black boxes" whose decisions are hard to justify .

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 5 Science, Tech & Environment › 19 › Big data, cloud computing, edge computing and data centres › Edge vs fog vs cloud computing - latency, use cases
bullets: Cloud: Where processing happens Distant centralised data centres; Use Heavy storage and analytics
Fog: Where processing happens Between the edge and the cloud, when edge devices lack power; Use Local aggregation
Edge: Where processing happens On or near the device; Use Lowest latency, real-time (e.g. a camera sends only suspicious clips)
Edge computing saves bandwidth and keeps sensitive data local. Reliance committed to a nationwide edge-computing network at the India AI summit (VIS PT365 2026).

bullets: Ashok Dalwai Committee (2016-18), 14 volumes; target 2022, base year 2015-16 .
Shift from "production" to "income": value addition, clusters, e-NAM/APMC reform, post-harvest infrastructure, livestock-fisheries integration, land-leasing laws.

sections.topic: Sources of institutional finance for AP farmers
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 3 Economy › C-5 › Institutional credit to agriculture in Andhra Pradesh - banks, NABARD and SHGs › Sources of institutional finance for AP farmers
bullets: AP farmers borrow from commercial banks, RRBs and PACS, i.e. all of them (PYQ 2008). Other formal sources are SHGs/JLGs, microfinance and KCC.
Nationally, scheduled commercial banks give over 70% of formal farm credit. The cooperative system (PACS-DCCB-SCB) gives short-term credit, and ARDBs give long-term credit (LENS Apr 2026).
AP Annual Credit Plan 2025-26 review (Jan 2026): Rs 2.96 lakh crore disbursed to agriculture and allied sectors, Rs 1,490 crore to tenant farmers and Rs 95,714 crore to MSMEs (TH, 24 Jan 2026).
Formal credit excludes many tenant, tribal, women and oral-lessee farmers because it needs land records. A NABARD Guntur study found formal interest rates of about 2.5-10%.
KCC (1998, NABARD model scheme on the R.V. Gupta Committee): RBI's revised KCC Directions of 19 Jun 2026 apply to loans from 1 Jan 2027, with a maximum tenure of 6 years (earlier 5).

bullets: Women's one-third is a compulsory provision; reservation for backward classes is voluntary (APP; CDI). Reserved seats may be allotted by rotation (APP).
73rd in force 24 April 1993; SC/ST reservation in local bodies lapses with Art. 334 (currently 2030) (CDI).
SC/ST seats at every level are in proportion to population. Chairperson offices are reserved as State law provides and allotted by rotation. States may reserve seats for BCs.

bullets: Education: better education brings better jobs and higher social standing; the emerging class system allows upward mobility (APP).
Reservation: backward classes in the South (Self-Respect Movement of Periyar) demanded reservation in government jobs; reservation led to group mobility (APP).
Reservation has also broadened the urban middle class by bringing in backward classes and Dalits (APP).
Occupational mobility: e.g., Ezhavas of Kerala moved from toddy tapping into tailoring and cottage industries (APP).
Migration and urbanisation: city anonymity and caste-blind public spaces weaken caste identity, but migrants carry caste networks and prejudices into cities (APP).

items.title: India’s Rising Supercomputing Ecosystem
items.summary: 04 OCT 2026 5:58PM by PIB Delhi India’s supercomputing journey has evolved from PARAM 8000 in the early 1990s to a national ecosystem under the National Supercomputing Mission (NSM), launched in 2015. With 40 supercomputers delivering 68 PF as of September 2026, NSM is expanding access to high-performance computing (HPC).

facts.text: 04 OCT 2026 5:58PM by PIB Delhi India’s supercomputing journey has evolved from PARAM 8000 in the early 1990s to a national ecosystem under the National Supercomputing Mission (NSM), launched in 2015.

The Mission has also developed indigenous servers, software, cooling and networking technologies, while supporting applications in Computational Biology, Weather Prediction and Climate Modelling, Disaster Management, Big Data Analytics, and Astrophysics.

The event will be held at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, under the theme “Creative Minds, Catalyzing Science, Empowering Technologies.” Organised by the Council of Scientific & Industrial Research (CSIR), ESTIC-2026 will advance emerging science and technology frontiers.
The Mission was launched with an outlay of about ₹ 4,500 crore .

items.title: Union Environment Minister releases two male Great Indian Bustards into the wild at Desert National Park, Jaisalmer
items.summary: Rajasthan State Minister for Forest and Environment, Shri Sanjay Sharma, along with senior officers of the Union and State Governments, was present on the occasion. In a post on X, Shri Yadav thanked Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi for his continued guidance, encouragement and support in enabling the scientific community to work towards the conservation of the Great Indian Bustard and other species.

facts.text: In a milestone move, released two male Great Indian Bustards in Sam, Desert National Park, Jaisalmer, today morning.
Of these 11, 2 birds were released into the wild at Desert National Park today.

These efforts are being reinforced through habitat restoration by the Rajasthan Forest Department, including the establishment of around 200 sq. km. of fenced grassland enclosures inside the Desert National Park.
The species’ conservation actions are being guided by the Judgement of the Supreme Court of India, based on recommendations of the Expert Committee constituted for this purpose.

bullets: AP farmers borrow from commercial banks, RRBs and PACS, i.e. all of them (PYQ 2008). Other formal sources are SHGs/JLGs, microfinance and KCC.
Nationally, scheduled commercial banks give over 70% of formal farm credit. The cooperative system (PACS-DCCB-SCB) gives short-term credit, and ARDBs give long-term credit (LENS Apr 2026).
AP Annual Credit Plan 2025-26 review (Jan 2026): Rs 2.96 lakh crore disbursed to agriculture and allied sectors, Rs 1,490 crore to tenant farmers and Rs 95,714 crore to MSMEs (TH, 24 Jan 2026).
Formal credit excludes many tenant, tribal, women and oral-lessee farmers because it needs land records. A NABARD Guntur study found formal interest rates of about 2.5-10%.
KCC (1998, NABARD model scheme on the R.V. Gupta Committee): RBI's revised KCC Directions of 19 Jun 2026 apply to loans from 1 Jan 2027, with a maximum tenure of 6 years (earlier 5).

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 3 Economy › C-3 › Indian agriculture - importance, land use classification, cropping seasons and cropping pattern › Agricultural census - size classes, women's share, largest holding state, AP holdings
bullets: India, 10th Agriculture Census (2015-16): 146 million holdings with an average size of 1.08 ha, down from 2.28 ha in 1971. Small and marginal holdings make up 86.2% of holdings but only 47.3% of the area (APPCA; UPSC).
Size classes above are the standard Agriculture Census classes ; "small and marginal farmers" = holdings up to 2 ha.
Tenth Agriculture Census 2015-16 (still the standard all-India reference): 146 million operational holdings, average size 1.08 ha, down from 2.28 ha in 1971 - fragmentation (APPCA 2026).
Small and marginal farmers are about 86.2% of all farmers but hold only about 47% of the crop area (APPCA, May 2026).
Eleventh Agriculture Census 2021-22: provisional State results out; All-India 2021-22 figures are not yet the standard reference.

items.title: In 1963, scientist swabbed his daughter’s throat; her virus strain led to a mumps vaccine in 1967
items.summary: In 1963, scientist Maurice Hilleman collected a mumps virus sample from his five-year-old daughter Jeryl Lynn. bullets: Stored water has potential energy; falling water gains kinetic energy, which spins the turbine (mechanical energy); the generator converts it to electrical energy by electromagnetic induction .
Run-of-the-river plants need no large dam/reservoir; they use the natural flow without much altering the watercourse.
Run-of-river: Feature Little or no storage; uses natural flow
Storage (reservoir): Feature Dam stores water, regulates output
Pumped storage: Feature Surplus power pumps water uphill; released at peak - a "grid battery", fastest large-scale storage (CDI)

bullets: Meaning: rising share of women in the agricultural workforce (as cultivators, labourers and unpaid family workers) while men move to non-farm and urban work.

Causes: male out-migration to cities; distress - low household income pushes rural women into low-productivity farm work; concentration of women in subsistence farming and unpaid family work (LENSD, 24 Aug 2026); COVID-era return migration made women intensify farm work (TH, 25 Jul 2026).

Women's WPR follows a U-shaped curve (Claudia Goldin): high in agriculture in the 1980s, fell with mechanisation 2004-05 to 2012, rising again after 2020 partly out of distress (TH, 25 Jul 2026).

IMD "Observed Rainfall Variability and Changes over Andhra Pradesh": climate hot and humid, summer March-June; rainfall variability quite high (APPSC 2025 key).
Retreating monsoon: withdraws October-November; Bay of Bengal cyclones bring the rain of this season to the southern states.
SW monsoon (June-September) gives ~2/3 (65-70%) of AP's rainfall. It sets in during the 2nd week of June; July is the wettest month (CDI; APP).
Normal rainfall (APSES 2024-25): SWM 574.7 mm + NEM 285.3 mm = ~860 mm a year. CDI prints a State average of ~966 mm (older figure). 2024: SWM 681.6 mm (+18.6%); NEM 278.7 mm (-2.3%).

bullets: The IHR (2005) are a legally binding WHO instrument, in force since 2007. Member states must build core capacities for surveillance and response, report possible PHEICs to WHO within 24 hours, and name a National IHR Focal Point .

bullets: It merges 9 laws (EPF, ESI, Maternity Benefit, Gratuity, Unorganised Workers' Social Security Act, etc.). The four Labour Codes came into force on 21 Nov 2025, with the 2026 Central Rules (CDI Block15).

It recognises gig workers, platform workers and aggregators in law for the first time. Aggregators pay 1-2% of annual turnover (capped at 5% of payouts) into a social security fund. A National Social Security Board recommends schemes (CDI; LENS Jul 2025). Maternity leave stays at 26 weeks; a creche is required at 50+ employees.

e-Shram (26 Aug 2021, MoLE): Aadhaar-verified National Database of Unorganised Workers; 12-digit UAN; age 16-59; excludes income-tax payers and EPFO/ESIC members. The 2024 One-Stop Solution joins up 15 schemes; 31.87 crore registered (LENSD, 26 Aug and 16 Aug 2026).

sections.topic: The universe and the solar system · Sun
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 4 Geography › D-1 › The universe and the solar system - origin theories, the Sun, planets, asteroids, comets, meteors › Sun - layers, surface temperature, size, sunspots, solar flares
bullets: Sunspots: cooler dark magnetic patches; 11-year cycle - matched by plasma currents in the 35,000-km-deep Near-Surface Shear Layer (LENS, May 2025).

Flares/CMEs hit satellites, GPS, aviation, radio, power grids; cause auroras . Aditya-L1 showed the Oct 2024 storm strongly compressed Earth's magnetic shield (TH, 11 Jan 2026). ESA-China SMILE (Vega-C) will image the solar wind-magnetosphere link (LENS, Apr 2026).
Sunspots: cooler, darker regions of intense magnetic activity; markers of the ~11-year solar cycle (minimum to maximum); the Sun's magnetic poles reverse at each peak (LENS Feb 2026).
Solar flares: sudden bursts of radiation from magnetic reconnection, classed A, B, C, M, X (X strongest). CMEs: plasma clouds from the corona at 250-3,000 km/s, reaching Earth in 1-3 days.
Effects on Earth: geomagnetic storms, auroras, damage to satellites, communication, navigation and power grids.

sections.where: Rocket Sheets · Physics › #17 · Electromagnetic Spectrum and Applications
bullets: The increasing-wavelength order of electromagnetic radiation is gamma rays, X-rays, ultraviolet, visible light, infrared, microwaves, and radio waves.
AM and FM radio and TV signals are applications of radio-wave broadcasting.
Radio waves are used for radar detection and ranging.
Ultraviolet markers on currency and documents help detect forgery.
X-rays are used to detect cracks in metals.

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 5 Science, Tech & Environment › 21 › Applications of radioisotopes in agriculture, medicine and industry › Medical radioisotopes - isotope, radiation and use
bullets: Iodine-131: Emits Beta + gamma; Use (diagnosis / therapy) Thyroid disorders - diagnosis and treatment; BRIT supplies it as sodium iodide (APP)
Phosphorus-32: Emits Beta; Use (diagnosis / therapy) Blood cancer (leukaemia) / polycythaemia treatment
Sodium-24: Emits Gamma; Use (diagnosis / therapy) Speed of blood flow, circulation blocks (UPPSC 2012 key: radio-sodium)
Iron-59: Emits Beta + gamma; Use (diagnosis / therapy) Iron metabolism, anaemia studies
Leukaemia keys vary: UPPSC 2012 accepted P-32 or Co-60, and BPSC 2016 marked "more than one". Blood-flow speed: Radio-Sodium (UPPSC 2012).

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 4 Geography › D-1 › Atmosphere - structure (layers) and composition › Ionosphere sub-layers (D, E, F) and communication role
bullets: Extends from about 60 km to over 1,000 km. Solar UV and X-rays strip electrons from atoms; charged particles cause auroras and airglow; it reflects radio waves back to Earth, which allows long-distance communication. It expands by day, shrinks at night; solar flares and geomagnetic storms disrupt GNSS signals (LENS daily, 9 Jul 2026).
E (Kennelly-Heaviside): Height ~90-150 km; Role Reflects medium-frequency radio waves
F (Appleton; F1, F2 by day): Height ~150 km upward; Role Main reflector of short-wave radio
Within the thermosphere, about 80-400 km; electrically charged ions reflect radio waves transmitted from Earth, making long-distance radio possible.
F (Appleton; F1, F2): Height ~150-400 km; Note Reflects short waves; key for long-distance radio

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 5 Science, Tech & Environment › 18 › Prominent Indian scientists - C.V. Raman, J.C. Bose, S.N. Bose, Ramanujan, Meghnad Saha, Homi Bhabha › J.C. Bose - inventions, plant-life work, institute, books
bullets: Showed that plants respond to stimuli like animals - "plants have life" (MPPSC 2015); invented the crescograph to measure plant growth .
Pioneer of microwave/millimetre-wave radio research - coherer and galena (semiconductor) detector .
Founded the Bose Institute, Kolkata (1917) ; worked at IACS (LENSD, 27 May 2026).
Books: *Response in the Living and Non-Living* (1902), *The Nervous Mechanism of Plants*; Bengali science fiction *Niruddesher Kahini* .

bullets: GloLitter Partnerships: run by IMO and FAO, funded by Norway, with India as a partner country. It targets sea-based marine plastic litter from shipping and fisheries . The APPSC-G1 2022 key treated a "UNEP initiative" statement as correct; the partnership is IMO-FAO.
Microplastics / microbeads: Meaning Plastic pieces < 5 mm; microbeads are added to cosmetics and scrubs

GloLitter Partnerships: by IMO and FAO (2019) to cut marine plastic litter from shipping and fishing (the APPSC 2022 key accepted "UNEP initiative" - some notes say UNEP; the project is IMO-FAO, funded by Norway ).
Microbeads: plastic particles < 5 mm in cosmetics ; ballast water moves invasive species - IMO BWM Convention (in force 2017) .
MARPOL 73/78 (IMO): 6 Annexes, bans plastic dumping at sea.

bullets: Oilzapper and Oilivorous-S: bacterial consortia developed by TERI (with Indian Oil ); degrade oily sludge and oil-contaminated sites, leaving no harmful residue (APP); used at Chennai port (CDI).
UPSC 2011: Oilzapper = eco-friendly technology for remediation of oily sludge and oil spills.
First GE oil-eating "superbug": *Pseudomonas putida* engineered by Ananda Mohan Chakrabarty; first living organism patented (*Diamond v. Chakrabarty*, US Supreme Court, 1980) .
